mergedParams.userDescription: Precision placement and spacing. internal effects for text, video, images

output.title: Precision Spacing & Internal Effects for Text, Video, Images

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'PrecisionGrid' that generates a sophisticated multi-stage positioning effect for arranging elements in mathematically precise grid formations. The effect should accept parameters for gridColumns, gridRows, spacing (in pixels), stagger (delay between elements), and alignment ('center', 'start', 'end'). It should return generic effects that animate elements from their initial scattered positions to precise grid coordinates using a spring-based easing. The effect should calculate each element's target position based on its index in targetIds array, applying translateX and translateY animations with progressive stagger timing. Include a secondary scale effect that makes elements pulse slightly (0.95 to 1.05) when they reach their final position, creating a satisfying 'lock-in' feel. The effect should also include an opacity fade-in that's synchronized with the movement.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (AnimationRange[]). Return format: { effects: [...] } with multiple effect objects. Each effect object: { type: 'generic', start: staggered based on index, duration: params.duration || 1000, mode: 'provider', targetIds: calculated per element, ranges: [{ key: 'translateX', val: calculated grid X, prog: [0, 1] }, { key: 'translateY', val: calculated grid Y, prog: [0, 1] }, { key: 'scale', val: [0.95, 1.05, 1], prog: [0.8, 0.9, 1] }, { key: 'opacity', val: [0, 1], prog: [0, 0.3] }], easing: 'spring' }. Input schema: z.object({ gridColumns: z.number(), gridRows: z.number(), spacing: z.number(), stagger: z.number(), alignment: z.enum(['center', 'start', 'end']), duration: z.number().optional() }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal waveform effect preset named 'BeatPrecisionZoom' that creates audio-reactive zoom pulses with surgical precision timing. The effect should react to bass frequencies for heavy beats, but with a unique twist - it should analyze the audio to detect the exact beat onset and apply a two-phase zoom: first a quick zoom-in (scale 1.0 to 1.15) on the beat hit, then a slower elastic bounce-back (1.15 to 0.98 to 1.0). Parameters should include sensitivity (0-1), targetScale (max zoom level), decaySpeed (how fast it returns), and frequencyRange ('bass', 'mid', 'treble'). The effect should use waveform data to calculate the intensity multiplier and apply it to the scale transformation. Include a subtle rotation effect (±3 degrees) that's inversely proportional to the zoom for added dynamism.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: waveform (audio-reactive). Return format: { effects: [waveformEffect] }. Effect object: { type: 'waveform', start: 0, duration: params.duration || 'auto', mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, props: { zoom: { enabled: true, type: 'bass', sensitivity: params.sensitivity || 0.7, threshold: 0.3, maxScale: params.targetScale || 1.15, decaySpeed: params.decaySpeed || 0.92 }, rotate: { enabled: true, type: 'bass', sensitivity: params.sensitivity * 0.3, maxRotation: 3, inverse: true } } }. Input schema: z.object({ targetIds: z.array(z.string()), sensitivity: z.number().min(0).max(1), targetScale: z.number().optional(), decaySpeed: z.number().optional(), frequencyRange: z.enum(['bass', 'mid', 'treble']).optional() }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset called 'TextKerningCascade' specifically for precise letter-spacing animations in text elements. The effect should animate individual characters' letterSpacing property to create a cascading expansion/contraction effect. It accepts parameters for startSpacing (initial letter-spacing in em units), endSpacing (final spacing), cascadeDirection ('left-to-right', 'right-to-left', 'center-out', 'random'), cascadeSpeed (ms delay between characters), and elasticity (bounce factor 0-1). The effect should calculate timing offsets for each character based on its position, creating a wave-like spacing adjustment that flows through the text. Include a complementary opacity effect where characters fade in as they reach their target spacing, and add a subtle translateY bounce (±5px) synchronized with the spacing change for dimensional depth.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (AnimationRange[]). Return format: { effects: [...] } with effect per character. Effect structure: { type: 'generic', start: index * params.cascadeSpeed, duration: 800, mode: 'provider', targetIds: [charId], ranges: [{ key: 'letterSpacing', val: [params.startSpacing, params.endSpacing * (1 + params.elasticity), params.endSpacing], prog: [0, 0.7, 1] }, { key: 'opacity', val: [0, 1], prog: [0, 0.4] }, { key: 'translateY', val: [0, -5, 0], prog: [0.3, 0.6, 1] }], easing: 'ease-out' }. Input schema: z.object({ targetIds: z.array(z.string()), startSpacing: z.number(), endSpacing: z.number(), cascadeDirection: z.enum(['left-to-right', 'right-to-left', 'center-out', 'random']), cascadeSpeed: z.number(), elasticity: z.number().min(0).max(1) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset named 'PrecisionClipPath' that uses CSS clip-path animations to reveal elements with geometric precision. The effect should support multiple reveal patterns: 'diagonal-wipe' (diagonal line sweeping across), 'iris' (circular expansion from center), 'blinds' (vertical strips revealing sequentially), 'polygon-morph' (morphing between polygon shapes). Parameters include revealType, duration, stagger (for multi-element reveals), direction (for applicable types), and smoothness (0-1 for animation curve refinement). The effect should generate clip-path polygon or circle values with precise mathematical calculations, ensuring pixel-perfect alignment. Add a complementary brightness filter that starts at 1.3 and fades to 1.0 as the clip-path completes, creating a subtle highlight effect on the revealed portions.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (AnimationRange[]). Return format: { effects: [...] }. Effect object: { type: 'generic', start: index * params.stagger || 0, duration: params.duration || 1200, mode: 'provider', targetIds: [elementId], ranges: [{ key: 'clipPath', val: calculateClipPathValues(params.revealType, params.direction), prog: generateProgressPoints(params.smoothness) }, { key: 'brightness', val: [1.3, 1.0], prog: [0, 1] }], easing: 'ease-in-out' }. Helper functions: calculateClipPathValues() returns array of clip-path strings based on type. Input schema: z.object({ targetIds: z.array(z.string()), revealType: z.enum(['diagonal-wipe', 'iris', 'blinds', 'polygon-morph']), duration: z.number().optional(), stagger: z.number().optional(), direction: z.string().optional(), smoothness: z.number().min(0).max(1) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal combined effect preset called 'MagneticSnap' that simulates magnetic attraction for precise element placement. When activated, elements should appear to be magnetically pulled to their target positions with physics-based movement. The effect combines multiple animation properties: first, elements slightly repel (scale down to 0.92, rotate ±5°) as if building magnetic tension, then snap to position with an accelerating translateX/Y curve, followed by a subtle overshoot and elastic settle. Parameters include attractionStrength (affects acceleration curve), snapDistance (threshold for magnetic effect), tensionDuration (pre-snap tension build), and magneticAxis ('both', 'horizontal', 'vertical'). Include a glow effect (box-shadow animation) that intensifies during attraction and pulses on snap completion.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: combined (multiple generic effects). Return format: { effects: [...tensionEffects, ...snapEffects, ...glowEffects] }. Tension effect: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.tensionDuration || 300, ranges: [{ key: 'scale', val: [1, 0.92], prog: [0, 1] }, { key: 'rotate', val: [0, randomSign() * 5], prog: [0, 1] }] }. Snap effect: { type: 'generic', start: params.tensionDuration, duration: 600, ranges: [{ key: 'translateX', val: calculateMagneticCurve(targetX, params.attractionStrength), prog: [0, 0.6, 0.8, 1] }, { key: 'scale', val: [0.92, 1.08, 0.97, 1], prog: [0, 0.5, 0.75, 1] }], easing: 'spring' }. Input schema: z.object({ targetIds: z.array(z.string()), targetPositions: z.array(z.object({ x: z.number(), y: z.number() })), attractionStrength: z.number().min(0).max(1), snapDistance: z.number(), tensionDuration: z.number().optional(), magneticAxis: z.enum(['both', 'horizontal', 'vertical']) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal waveform effect preset named 'FrequencySpacingOscillator' that dynamically adjusts element spacing based on audio frequency analysis. This effect should monitor specific frequency bands and translate their intensity into precise spacing adjustments between elements. Parameters include frequencyBands (array of frequency ranges to monitor), spacingMultiplier (base spacing adjustment factor), oscillationMode ('expand-contract', 'wave', 'random'), smoothing (0-1 for movement smoothness), and anchorPoint ('center', 'start', 'end' for spacing origin). The effect should calculate real-time position adjustments for each element based on frequency data, creating organic spacing rhythms. Include a complementary opacity modulation that's inversely related to spacing (elements fade slightly when spread apart) and a subtle blur effect that increases with rapid spacing changes.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: waveform (audio-reactive). Return format: { effects: [...] } with effect per element. Effect object: { type: 'waveform', start: 0, duration: 'auto', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [elementId], props: { translate: { enabled: true, type: 'frequency', frequencyRange: params.frequencyBands[index % params.frequencyBands.length], sensitivity: 0.8, smoothing: params.smoothing || 0.7, translateX: calculateSpacingOffset(index, params.spacingMultiplier, params.anchorPoint), translateY: 0 }, opacity: { enabled: true, type: 'frequency', inverse: true, minOpacity: 0.7, maxOpacity: 1 }, blur: { enabled: true, type: 'frequency', maxBlur: 2, threshold: 0.6 } } }. Input schema: z.object({ targetIds: z.array(z.string()), frequencyBands: z.array(z.array(z.number())), spacingMultiplier: z.number(), oscillationMode: z.enum(['expand-contract', 'wave', 'random']), smoothing: z.number().min(0).max(1), anchorPoint: z.enum(['center', 'start', 'end']) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'PerspectiveStack' that arranges elements in precise 3D space with depth-based positioning. The effect should transform flat elements into a layered stack with accurate perspective, where each element has calculated translateZ values and complementary scale adjustments to maintain visual size. Parameters include stackDepth (total Z distance), layerSpacing (Z distance between elements), perspectiveOrigin ('center', 'top', 'bottom', 'left', 'right'), rotateX/Y (for tilted stacks), and fadeDepth (opacity reduction for distant elements). The effect should apply transform3d with precise calculations, ensuring elements maintain their relative positions while creating convincing depth. Include a hover-activated focus effect where elements temporarily move forward in Z-space when targeted.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (AnimationRange[]). Return format: { effects: [...] } with stacked positioning. Effect object: { type: 'generic', start: index * 50, duration: 1000, mode: 'provider', targetIds: [elementId], ranges: [{ key: 'transform', val: `perspective(1000px) translateZ(${-index * params.layerSpacing}px) rotateX(${params.rotateX}deg) rotateY(${params.rotateY}deg) scale(${calculatePerspectiveScale(index)})`, prog: [0, 1] }, { key: 'opacity', val: [0, calculateDepthOpacity(index, params.fadeDepth)], prog: [0, 0.5] }, { key: 'filter', val: [`blur(${index * 0.5}px)`, 'blur(0px)'], prog: [0, 1] }], easing: 'ease-out' }. Input schema: z.object({ targetIds: z.array(z.string()), stackDepth: z.number(), layerSpacing: z.number(), perspectiveOrigin: z.enum(['center', 'top', 'bottom', 'left', 'right']), rotateX: z.number().optional(), rotateY: z.number().optional(), fadeDepth: z.number().min(0).max(1) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset named 'GridMorph' that precisely transforms elements between different grid layouts. The effect should smoothly animate elements from one grid configuration (e.g., 3x3) to another (e.g., 2x4) with calculated position interpolation. Parameters include startGrid (columns/rows), endGrid (columns/rows), morphDuration, morphCurve ('linear', 'ease', 'bounce', 'elastic'), gapTransition (how spacing changes), and preserveAspectRatio (boolean). The effect should calculate intermediate positions for each element during the morph, ensuring no collisions and maintaining visual flow. Add a rotational twist during transition (elements rotate 180° then back) and a color shift effect that visualizes the morphing process through hue rotation.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (AnimationRange[]). Return format: { effects: [...] } for grid transformation. Effect object: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.morphDuration || 1500, mode: 'provider', targetIds: [elementId], ranges: [{ key: 'translateX', val: calculateMorphPath(startX, endX, params.morphCurve), prog: generateCurvePoints(params.morphCurve) }, { key: 'translateY', val: calculateMorphPath(startY, endY, params.morphCurve), prog: generateCurvePoints(params.morphCurve) }, { key: 'rotate', val: [0, 180, 360], prog: [0, 0.5, 1] }, { key: 'filter', val: ['hue-rotate(0deg)', 'hue-rotate(180deg)', 'hue-rotate(360deg)'], prog: [0, 0.5, 1] }], easing: params.morphCurve }. Input schema: z.object({ targetIds: z.array(z.string()), startGrid: z.object({ columns: z.number(), rows: z.number() }), endGrid: z.object({ columns: z.number(), rows: z.number() }), morphDuration: z.number().optional(), morphCurve: z.enum(['linear', 'ease', 'bounce', 'elastic']), gapTransition: z.number(), preserveAspectRatio: z.boolean() }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal combined effect preset called 'TypewriterPrecision' that creates a precise character-by-character reveal with mechanical typewriter aesthetics. Unlike simple opacity reveals, this effect should simulate actual typewriter mechanics: each character appears with a slight overshoot (scale 1.2 to 1.0), a subtle horizontal jitter (translateX ±2px), and a brief brightness flash. Parameters include typeSpeed (ms per character), caretVisible (show typing cursor), mechanicalJitter (0-1 for randomness), ribbonFade (simulates ink density variation), and pauseOnPunctuation (adds realistic pauses). The effect should handle word-wrapping awareness, ensuring characters don't appear mid-wrap. Include a paper texture overlay effect that subtly shifts as typing progresses, and authentic typewriter sound sync points.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: combined (multiple generic effects per character). Return format: { effects: [...appearEffects, ...jitterEffects, ...caretEffects] }. Appear effect: { type: 'generic', start: calculateTypeDelay(index, params.typeSpeed, params.pauseOnPunctuation), duration: 100, mode: 'provider', targetIds: [charId], ranges: [{ key: 'scale', val: [1.2, 1.0], prog: [0, 1] }, { key: 'opacity', val: [0, 1], prog: [0, 0.3] }, { key: 'brightness', val: [1.5, 1.0], prog: [0, 1] }] }. Jitter effect: { type: 'generic', start: same, duration: 50, ranges: [{ key: 'translateX', val: [0, randomJitter(), 0], prog: [0, 0.5, 1] }] }. Input schema: z.object({ targetIds: z.array(z.string()), typeSpeed: z.number(), caretVisible: z.boolean(), mechanicalJitter: z.number().min(0).max(1), ribbonFade: z.boolean(), pauseOnPunctuation: z.boolean() }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal waveform effect preset named 'HarmonicAlignment' that uses audio harmonic analysis to create precise geometric arrangements. The effect should detect harmonic frequencies in the audio and map them to mathematical positioning patterns - when certain harmonics align, elements snap into perfect geometric formations (golden ratio spirals, Fibonacci sequences, sacred geometry patterns). Parameters include harmonicSensitivity, geometryType ('golden-spiral', 'fibonacci', 'flower-of-life', 'metatron'), formationSpeed (how quickly elements move to formation), harmonicThreshold (minimum harmonic strength to trigger), and scaleWithIntensity (whether formation size relates to audio intensity). The effect should continuously analyze audio harmonics and smoothly transition between chaotic and ordered states. Include a complementary glow effect that intensifies when harmonic alignment is achieved, and a subtle particle trail effect showing movement paths.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: waveform (audio-reactive with harmonic analysis). Return format: { effects: [...] } with dynamic positioning. Effect object: { type: 'waveform', start: 0, duration: 'auto', mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, props: { translate: { enabled: true, type: 'harmonic', harmonicAnalysis: true, sensitivity: params.harmonicSensitivity, geometryFunction: getGeometryPosition(params.geometryType, index, harmonicData), smoothing: 0.85, formationSpeed: params.formationSpeed }, scale: { enabled: params.scaleWithIntensity, type: 'harmonic', minScale: 0.8, maxScale: 1.2 }, glow: { enabled: true, type: 'harmonic', glowIntensity: 'auto', color: 'harmonicColor' } } }. Input schema: z.object({ targetIds: z.array(z.string()), harmonicSensitivity: z.number().min(0).max(1), geometryType: z.enum(['golden-spiral', 'fibonacci', 'flower-of-life', 'metatron']), formationSpeed: z.number(), harmonicThreshold: z.number(), scaleWithIntensity: z.boolean() }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects', dependencies: { presets: ['harmonic-analyzer'] } }
